name: Royal Trux
label: Drag City
lede: Neil Hagerty left Pussy Galore's day job for a band with Jennifer Herrema, cut a double LP in San Francisco, gave Drag City its first record, and took more than $1 million from Virgin. Years after splitting, a Guardian interview ended the reunion.

eras.title: Out of Pussy Galore
eras.text: Neil Hagerty was a teenage guitarist in Jon Spencer's Pussy Galore, the D.C. noise band that treated rock history like scrap metal. On the side he and Jennifer Herrema, still in her teens, started a band that would outlast the day job.

years.h: Neil Hagerty talks [[Pussy Galore|cf97d78e-7c86-4931-92c0-b8e22bae1e33]] into remaking Exile on Main St.
years.p: Still a teenager, Hagerty gets Jon Spencer's band to record a full cassette-only version of the Rolling Stones' double album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Royal Trux · Stereogum: Royal Trux albums
years.h: Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema start Royal Trux in Washington
years.p: He's in his early twenties, she's in her late teens. Hagerty treats Pussy Galore as the job and Royal Trux as the real thing.

years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: The debut comes out on the band's own Royal label
years.p: Royal Trux is Hagerty and Herrema's songs sawn into pieces and stuck back together; Stereogum calls it ramshackle.

eras.title: The band Drag City started with
eras.text: Two Chicago record fans, Dan Koretzky and Dan Osborn, started Drag City after hearing Royal Trux, and the band gave the label its first single and its first album. Hagerty and Herrema then helped steer Will Oldham to the roster.

years.h: Drag City's first record is a Royal Trux 7-inch
years.p: Dan Koretzky and Dan Osborn start the label after hearing the band, and Hero/Zero is the first release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twin Infinitives · Stereogum: Royal Trux albums
yt: Live at the Middle East, Cambridge MA, 1989
years.h: Drag City's first full-length is a double LP cut in San Francisco
years.p: Recorded October 1989 to June 1990 at Lowdown, Twin Infinitives runs fifteen songs over four sides, including the 14-minute (Edge of the) Ape Oven.
years.xp:
The couple were living near the poverty line in San Francisco. Stereogum says they tracked the album completely sober, then reviewed the mixes under various substances, a marijuana test and an LSD test among them.

NME and Uncut gave it 9/10. Drowned in Sound gave it 5.

years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: Untitled, which fans call the Skulls record
years.p: Royal Trux's third album is their first built from conventional songs, tracked on an 8-track. Stereogum calls it the band's first clean record.

years.h: Bill Callahan's first tour is with Royal Trux
years.p: Callahan, then recording as [[Smog|89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34]], co-headlines with the band in 1992. Neil Hagerty later produces Callahan records.

years.h: Royal Trux help get Will Oldham onto Drag City
years.p: Hagerty and Herrema are among those who convince the label to sign [[Palace|44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8]]'s Oldham, and they produce the Palace Brothers single Come In as Adam and Eve.

years.cap: Royal Trux at the Mean Fiddler, Harlesden, London, 1993
years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: Kurt Cobain is said to be a fan of Cats and Dogs
years.p: Royal Trux add guitarist Michael Kaiser and drummer Ian Willers. Stereogum ranks the album first, "the centerpiece of the Trux oeuvre."

years.cap: Jennifer Herrema with Royal Trux at the Mean Fiddler, London, 1993
years.h: "Axl Rose!" shouts the Lollapalooza crowd at Herrema
years.p: Royal Trux play the 1993 festival's side stage, and Jennifer Herrema has to take the heckling.

eras.title: A million dollars of Virgin money
eras.text: After Nirvana, major labels went shopping for indie credibility, and Virgin signed Royal Trux. The money bought a house and studio in rural Virginia, a real rhythm section and a clean break from heroin. It didn't buy the record Virgin wanted.

years.src: Wikipedia: Royal Trux · Stereogum: Royal Trux albums
years.h: Virgin signs Royal Trux for over $1 million
years.p: The deal covers three albums, and the label wants indie credibility now that Nirvana has broken.
years.xp: The duo bought a house in Virginia and turned it into a studio, where they also recorded other bands, [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]] among them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Royal Trux · Stereogum: Royal Trux albums
years.h: Neil Young's producer David Briggs runs Thank You
years.p: Royal Trux cut it almost completely live with [[David Briggs|49b65db4-fe20-4a97-9073-55d33e65ac98]], plus bassist Dan Brown and drummer Chris Pyle, son of [[Lynyrd Skynyrd|c544ed4d-2390-4442-a83e-1ea2883b09c8]]'s Artimus Pyle.
years.xp: Stereogum puts the sessions at Joe Walsh's Kiva Studios in Nashville, and ranks the album seventh.

years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: Virgin hears Sweet Sixteen and objects to the sleeve
years.p: Recorded at the band's Virginia ranch studio. Stereogum says the cover, a toilet bowl, was the sticking point.
years.xp: Stereogum ranks it fourth and calls it "their Abbey Road or Pet Sounds." Herrema said afterward she was "continually impressed" that she took part in it.

years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: Royal Trux turn down a third Virgin album and keep the check
years.p: Stereogum says the label cut them loose with "a fat severance check," which paid for the next album.

years.h: Neil Hagerty puts out a science-fiction novel, Victory Chimp
years.p: It appears the same year as Sweet Sixteen.

eras.title: Home to Drag City, then apart
eras.text: Back on Drag City with Virgin's check in the bank, Royal Trux made three records in three years, their most straight-up rock. Then the couple's relationship ended on the road, and the band ended with it.

years.h: Bobby Gillespie names a song after Accelerator
years.p: Royal Trux return to Drag City and add keyboardist Tim McClain. [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]'s Gillespie calls a track Accelerator on 2000's XTRMNTR.
years.xp: Stereogum calls the Primal Scream song an "obvious homage." It also says the Royal Trux album leans on a device called the Spectrum Analyzer and on 1980s sounds.

years.h: Jon Theodore and David Pajo join for Veterans of Disorder
years.p: Future [[The Mars Volta|20883363-1ea4-4d72-ad72-c0e767038f3e]] drummer [[Jon Theodore|eeb1d415-4dbc-4038-8b09-4faf8c3c24ba]] and [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]]'s [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]], on bass, back the band on the record.
years.xp: Stereogum hears it as a run of singles, opening on the riff of Waterpark and closing with Blue Is the Frequency.

q: You have to really like music to like our band
years.h: Hagerty puts the band's audience in one sentence
years.p: Stereogum dates the line to a late-1990s interview. The band, it adds, "couldn't care less" if it lost an audience and gained a new one with each album.

years.h: Pound for Pound picks up where Blue Is the Frequency stops
years.p: The band called the album an extension of that closer on Veterans of Disorder. It's the last record of the first run.

years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux albums · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: The couple split on tour, and Royal Trux goes with them
years.p: The relationship comes apart on the 2000 Pound for Pound tour; Stereogum ties it to Herrema's relapses after her father's death. The band ends in 2001.

years.h: Hagerty goes to the Howling Hex, Herrema to RTX
years.p: Both stay on Drag City. Hagerty records solo and as [[The Howling Hex|beb385d7-b5d9-41a9-a75a-6ac94dcf1c44]]; Herrema forms [[RTX|e7720ff7-d4f9-4cfb-ba39-c00e63572d13]], later [[Black Bananas|7fa9cc77-c2fa-4b4c-985a-6707d1794af8]].

eras.title: Reunion, then "I'm out, man"
eras.text: Fourteen years after the split, the two went back on stage together, made a first studio album in nineteen years, and fell apart in public before the tour could start.

years.cap: Royal Trux at Levitation Chicago, March 2016
years.h: Fourteen years after the split, Royal Trux play Berserktown
years.p: Hagerty and Herrema share a stage again at the festival in Santa Ana, California.

years.h: Webster Hall, New York, is the reunion's second date
years.p: The December 19 show follows August's set in Santa Ana.

years.cap: Royal Trux at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, June 2017
years.h: Platinum Tips + Ice Cream captures the reunion shows
years.p: The live album comes out in 2017; in May the band play their first UK date since reuniting, at Manchester's Victoria Warehouse.

years.h: Fat Possum puts the whole Royal Trux catalog on streaming
years.p: The band leave Drag City in early 2018 for the Mississippi label, and the entire discography reaches streaming for the first time.

years.cap: Jennifer Herrema at the keyboard, American Turners Club, Louisville, September 22, 2017
years.src: Stereogum: Royal Trux reschedule · Wikipedia: Royal Trux
years.h: Nineteen years after Pound for Pound, White Stuff
years.p: Royal Trux release their first studio album since 2000 on Fat Possum.
years.xp: The tour was in trouble before the record came out. Stereogum reported on January 15 that dates planned for February were postponed over unresolved issues from a past arrest of Herrema's. Her line in the press release about avoiding jail: "Shit could definitely be worse."

years.h: Hagerty is out, and the White Stuff tour is called off
years.p: He tells the Guardian he isn't touring and didn't approve the album. On April 30 the dates are cancelled, and both say the reunion is over.
years.xp: Hagerty said Herrema had steamrollered him: "She steamrollered right over me, man." He said he had no idea what the album was. Herrema answered that he regularly threatened to quit mid-tour. Both have said the reunion ended with White Stuff.
